text: You have twenty minutes before a call. Editing a draft needs twenty uninterrupted minutes; replying to messages takes five. Which plan finishes the draft before the call?
choices: Edit for ten minutes, reply, then finish
explanation: Editing now uses the full twenty-minute window. Replying first leaves fifteen minutes; interrupting the edit also breaks its uninterrupted requirement.

text: The shared folder contains Draft 3 and Draft 4. A message says, “I corrected the figures in Draft 4; the conclusion is unchanged.” Which file should a reviewer use for the corrected figures?
choices: Draft 3, because the conclusion is unchanged
Draft 4, where the figures were corrected
Either file; the figures must match
explanation: The message distinguishes the corrected figures from the unchanged conclusion. Only Draft 4 is identified as containing those corrections.

text: A workshop has two rooms. One holds eight people with a screen; the other holds twelve without a screen. Nine people need a screen, and furniture cannot move. What does this tell the organizer?
choices: The twelve-seat room meets both needs
The eight-seat room meets both needs
Neither room meets both needs as arranged
explanation: One room lacks a seat; the other lacks a screen. More capacity alone does not satisfy both requirements.

text: A portal always shows a receipt for a submitted report, and receipts stay visible. Noor sees no receipt for hers. Under these stated rules, what follows?
choices: Her report is not recorded as submitted
Her report was rejected after submission
The reviewer has not opened her report
explanation: A submitted report would have a visible receipt. The absence establishes submission status, not a reviewer decision or reading status.

text: A recipe uses two cups of rice for four servings. You need six servings, keeping the same ratio. Which amount fits?
explanation: Each serving uses half a cup. Six servings therefore need three cups.

text: The pickup note says, “Your parcel is in locker 12. The shop counter only handles returns.” You want to collect this parcel. Where should you go?
choices: The counter to ask for the parcel
explanation: The note assigns collection to locker 12 and returns to the counter. They serve different purposes.

text: A refill sign says, “Same cup, same day, receipt required.” You have today’s receipt but brought yesterday’s cup instead of the cup on that receipt. Which condition is missing?
choices: Using the cup from today’s purchase
explanation: The receipt and date meet two conditions. The cup must also be the one associated with that purchase.

text: The community library accepts returns through a slot all day, but loans require a volunteer from 2 to 5. You arrive at noon with one borrowed book and want another. What can you do immediately?
explanation: The return slot is available at noon. Borrowing must wait until the volunteer arrives at 2.

text: Ari can meet Monday or Tuesday; Bo can meet Tuesday or Wednesday. Cam is available only Tuesday. Which day works for everyone?
explanation: Tuesday is in all three availability lists. The other days each exclude at least one person.

text: Jo writes, “If the film starts after eight, save me a seat. Before eight, I am still on the train.” The screening starts at 8:30. What has Jo asked the group to do?
explanation: The screening meets Jo’s stated condition: it starts after eight. The request is to save a seat.

text: Minh says, “I can bring dessert, but I cannot bring anything that needs a fridge.” The host offers ice cream that must stay frozen, or biscuits that keep at room temperature. Which fits Minh’s offer?
choices: Ice cream, because it is dessert
Biscuits, because they need no fridge
explanation: Both are desserts, but only the biscuits also satisfy the no-fridge condition.

text: A message says, “I like the café idea; I still need to check whether I’m free.” What is confirmed?
choices: The person likes the idea, but attendance is undecided
explanation: Enthusiasm for the idea is explicit. Availability has not yet been checked, so attendance is not confirmed.

text: A lamp casts a sculpture’s shadow west. In this setup the shadow falls directly away from the lamp. Which side is the lamp on?
explanation: Westward shadow means light comes from the opposite side, east.

text: A photo shows empty chairs after a concert. The caption says only, “Ten minutes after the last song.” Which statement is supported without inventing a reason?
choices: The chairs were empty ten minutes after the last song
explanation: The image and caption establish the scene and timing. They do not reveal attendance earlier or how people felt.

text: A poster brief says, “Keep the title above the photo, and the date below the photo.” In a draft the date sits between the title and the photo. What needs moving?
choices: Move the title below the photo
Move the photo below the date
Move the date below the photo
explanation: The title already belongs above the photo. Moving the date below the photo restores the required order.

text: A short film needs thirty seconds of continuous music. Three clips are twenty seconds, thirty-five seconds, and forty seconds. You can trim but cannot join clips. Of the three original clips, which is the shortest that can supply the music?
explanation: Twenty seconds is too short. Both longer clips can be trimmed to thirty seconds, and thirty-five is the shorter of those.

text: On a map, the market is directly north of the library. The café is directly east of the library. From the café, which direction leads toward the market?
explanation: From the café, the market lies north and west: northwest.

text: Bus A serves the museum but not the station. Bus B serves the station but not the museum. Both stop at Central. Starting at the station, which route reaches the museum?
choices: Take A from the station, then B
Stay on B all the way
Take B to Central, then A
explanation: Bus B can take you from the station to the shared stop. Bus A then connects that stop to the museum.

text: A gallery normally closes at six. Today’s sign says, “Open until eight for exhibition night; last entry thirty minutes before closing.” When is today’s last entry?
explanation: Today’s special closing time is eight, so last entry is thirty minutes earlier, at seven thirty.

text: You reach a station at 10:10. The express leaves at 10:20 and takes twenty minutes; the local leaves now and takes thirty-five. Ignoring other delays, which gets you there first?
choices: The local, because it leaves now
explanation: The express arrives at 10:40, including its wait. The local arrives at 10:45, so the express wins by five minutes.

text: A sensor records an alert only when a room is below its light threshold. An alert appears at noon. What can the alert establish?
choices: The room was below the set light threshold
explanation: The alert establishes the measured light level. It does not identify the cause, such as weather or windows.

text: A clock loses one minute every hour. It is set correctly at noon. Three real hours later, what time will it show?
explanation: Three hours pass, but the clock loses three minutes. It shows three minutes before three: 2:57.

text: A photo file was created on Monday when an old print was scanned. The print has no date. What can Monday’s file date tell you?
choices: The original photo was taken Monday
The digital file was made Monday
The print was first developed Monday
explanation: The file date records the scanning result, not when the original scene was photographed or the print developed.

text: A display shows twelve objects. A sign says that every wooden object is handmade. Four objects are wooden. What is the smallest number we know are handmade?
choices: None, because the others are unknown
explanation: The four wooden objects are guaranteed handmade. Others might be handmade too, but the sign does not establish that.
